name: Hibatullah Akhundzada
role: Supreme leader of the Taliban and of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan (since 2016)
summary: Hibatullah Akhundzada, supreme leader of the Taliban since 2016, rules Afghanistan from Kandahar by decree, rejects democracy and Western law in favour of his reading of Sharia, and has approved bans on girls' secondary education, a strict dress and conduct code for women and a ban on poppy cultivation.

sources.title: From Land-grabbing to Haircuts: The decrees and edicts of the Taleban supreme leader (Afghanistan Analysts Network, 2023)
sources.author: Kate Clark
sources.usedFor: Analysis of his 65 published orders 2016-2023: his orders are the law, no parliament, the 2004 constitution suspended, the Sharia hijab order of April 2022, the poppy ban of April 2022, approval of hudud and qisas, the December 2021 women's-rights decree.

sources.title: Taliban enact law that silences Afghan women in public, and curbs their freedom (VOA, 22 Aug 2024)
sources.author: Voice of America
sources.usedFor: The 35-article Vice and Virtue law, published after his approval: women's faces and bodies covered, women's voices barred in public, music and images of living beings banned.

sources.title: Taliban supreme leader claims to have freed women from 'oppressions' in Eid message (KabulNow, June 2023)
sources.author: KabulNow
sources.usedFor: His Eid al-Adha 2023 message: steps for women 'according to the Islamic Sharia', Sharia courts and qisas.

sources.title: Taliban Chief Vows to Keep 'Laws of Infidels' From Afghanistan (VOA, April 2023)
sources.author: Voice of America
sources.usedFor: His April 2023 speech: an Islamic Sharia system, 'not a single law of infidelity' in Afghanistan.

sources.title: Taliban leader says there is no need for Western laws in Afghanistan (AP via Arab News, 2025)
sources.author: Associated Press
sources.usedFor: His Eid al-Fitr 2025 address: no laws from the West, democracy at an end, sharia in effect.

sources.title: Taliban Leader Calls U.S. the 'Greatest Oppressor' and 'Killer of Palestinian Muslims' (KabulNow, June 2025)
sources.author: KabulNow
sources.usedFor: His Eid al-Adha 2025 speech: democracy is not the way to save humanity, Islam and Sharia are.

sources.title: Situation of human rights in Afghanistan: report of the Special Rapporteur Richard Bennett (A/79/330, 30 Aug 2024), United Nations General Assembly
sources.author: UN Special Rapporteur on Afghanistan
sources.usedFor: Records that the Supreme Leader approved the Vice and Virtue law and reaffirmed public flogging and stoning in March 2024; girls barred beyond sixth grade; women shut out of political processes; all judges men; sodomy sentences by the Supreme Court; opium ban.

sources.title: Report on the implementation, enforcement and impact of the PVPV law (UNAMA, 10 April 2025)
sources.author: UNAMA
sources.usedFor: The law approved by the Taliban leader on 10 July 2024 and published 21 August 2024: its prohibitions on adultery, prostitution, homosexuality and sodomy, music and images of living beings, women's hijab and voices.

sources.title: Afghan supreme leader orders full enforcement of Islamic law (AFP via Arab News, 14 Nov 2022)
sources.author: Agence France-Presse
sources.usedFor: His November 2022 order, relayed by spokesman Mujahid after he met judges, obliging them to implement hudud and qisas sentences, including public executions, stonings, floggings and amputations.

sources.title: Taliban Ban Afghan Political Parties, Citing Sharia Violations (VOA, 16 Aug 2023)
sources.author: Voice of America
sources.usedFor: The Ministry of Justice's announcement that all political parties are banned for lack of any Sharia basis.

sources.title: The Taliban's first decree on women's rights makes no mention of education or work (Rukhshana Media, Dec 2021)
sources.author: Rukhshana Media
sources.usedFor: His 2 December 2021 decree: adult women's consent to marriage, a woman is not property, widows' inheritance and mahr, polygamists must treat wives justly.

sources.title: Taliban affirms that stoning will be punishment for adulterers, especially women (NPR via MPR News, 8 May 2024)
sources.author: NPR
sources.usedFor: His audio message of 24 March 2024: 'we will flog the women ... we will stone them to death in public'.

notFound.work: Full texts of his Eid messages and speeches (Pashto, Dari or English originals) and the Official Gazette decree texts

tried.how: only press reports with short quotations turned up; Dawn and Afghan Witness refused automated fetches (403) and were not retried

notes: First audit. He rarely appears in public and his recorded words are a few Eid addresses and messages, known through press reports with short quotations; the AAN study of his published orders and the 2024 Vice and Virtue law give the record of actions. Statements on which the sources hold nothing (death penalty, women's suffrage, minorities, trade, alliances and most economic questions) stay null. The December 2021 decree on women's rights is known from press summaries of its six points, not its text. Revision 2026-11-13: after the integrator's review, the UN Special Rapporteur report A/79/330, UNAMA's 2025 report on the Vice and Virtue law, the November 2022 order to judges, the 2023 party ban and the 2021 decree were added. The statements on the girls' education ban and on women's work have no statement in the bank to answer. Punish-blasphemy and wife-divorce-without-consent are null: none of these sources states a position or a rule. Dawn and Afghan Witness refused automated fetches and were not retried.
